job.style: a conversation between a teacher and two students

response.passage: In the science lab, Mr. Sharma asked Rohan and Meera to discuss energy. Rohan pointed to a battery, saying, 'The battery creates energy to power this toy car.' Mr. Sharma corrected him, explaining that energy is never created or destroyed; it is only transformed from one form to another. Meera then asked about a coolie walking on a flat platform with a heavy suitcase. She thought he was doing work because he was tired. Mr. Sharma clarified that scientific work requires a displacement in the direction of the force. Since the coolie's force is upward and the displacement is horizontal, the work done on the suitcase is zero. Rohan then wondered if a car’s kinetic energy doubles when its speed doubles. Mr. Sharma explained that kinetic energy is proportional to the square of the velocity, so doubling the speed actually quadruples the energy. Finally, they discussed a ball rolling to a stop. Meera asked if the energy vanished. Mr. Sharma explained that the energy is not destroyed; it is converted into heat due to friction with the floor. Energy is a conserved quantity that simply changes its form, whether in a battery, a moving car, or a rolling ball.
response.summary: Energy is a conserved quantity that is transformed rather than created or destroyed. Scientific work is only done when force causes displacement in the same direction. Kinetic energy increases exponentially with speed, not linearly.

items.evidence: energy is never created or destroyed; it is only transformed from one form to another.
items.stem: What happens to energy when a battery powers a toy car?

options.why: Student believes the battery is the source of energy creation.
Student thinks energy disappears after use.
Student thinks energy only exists in living things.

items.stem: How much scientific work is done by the coolie carrying the suitcase?

options.why: Student equates physical exhaustion with doing work.
Student believes carrying a load horizontally is work.
Student thinks work must be positive because it is scalar.

items.stem: What happens to the kinetic energy of a car if its speed is doubled?

options.why: Student assumes a linear relationship between speed and energy.
Student confuses speed with the rate of work.
Student incorrectly applies path dependence to energy.

items.stem: Where does the energy of a rolling ball go when it stops?

options.why: Student believes energy is destroyed when motion stops.
Student thinks energy becomes zero on the ground.
Student confuses energy dissipation with power units.
